project.name: The Quiet Lamp of Harrowmere — 쇼케이스 샘플
project.description: An original harbour-town missing-person mystery in four chapters (English → Korean), written for this repository. It carries only lines, speakers and the dialogue graph: characters, relationships, events, terms and speech rules are left empty so the workbench workflows can extract them. Scene order follows the story; the text is not taken from any game, book or film.

groups.title: Tidewatch office: tea and the Mooring Ledger
Notebook, day one
groups.description: The player writing in the notebook: nobody is spoken to.

groups.title: Lowtide Market: fish, rope and one notebook
The Brine Steps: Pippa and old Tarn
Town crier at the Brine Steps
groups.description: A public announcement: nobody in particular is addressed.

groups.title: Gull Lamp radio, evening sign-on
groups.description: Broadcast from the Gull Lamp on Skerrin Rock: addressed to every listener.

groups.title: Net-Menders' Union hall: the night of the gale
groups.description: The long group scene: the whole cast shelters from the storm; the person being spoken to changes almost every line.

groups.title: The Brine Steps in the gale
Tidewatch gate, morning after the gale
The grey cabinet: pages gone from the Mooring Ledger
Dunnock Quay, midnight: Hollis lets go
groups.description: The turning point: from stiff formality to first names.

groups.title: Town crier, reward notice
groups.description: A public notice; the crier speaks to the whole square.

units.speaker: FERRY CLERK
units.source: Last call for Harrowmere, folks! Have your tickets out.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Excuse me. I have a Tidewatch voucher, not a ticket. Is that all right?

units.speaker: FERRY CLERK
units.source: Tidewatch, is it? Hold on, I'll find the stamp for that.

units.speaker: FERRY CLERK
units.source: There. Mind the plank, it bounces.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Thank you. Is the sea always this grey?

units.speaker: FERRY CLERK
units.source: Grey? This is a cheerful day. Wait for the gale season.

units.speaker: PASSERBY 1
units.source: Another new face. That's the third this month.

units.speaker: PASSERBY 2
units.source: Shh. She's Tidewatch. Look at the coat.
The ferry horn sounds twice, long and low.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Constable {player} Reeve, first posting. Deep breath, and do not trip on the plank.

units.speaker: FERRY CLERK
units.source: Harrowmere in ten minutes! Hold your hats, and hold your stomachs!

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Constable Reeve. You are eleven minutes behind the timetable.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: The ferry was held for a cargo check, Inspector. I apologise.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Do not apologise to me. Apologise to the tide. It waits for nobody.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Dorian Hollis, Inspector of the Harrowmere Tidewatch. You will use the title.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Yes, Inspector. Constable {player} Reeve, reporting for duty.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Your file says you finished first in your class. This is not a classroom.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: No, sir. I understand.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Inspector. Not "sir." Sir is for schoolmasters.

units.speaker: FISHMONGER
units.source: Oi, Old Gull! Is that the new one? She looks about twelve!

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Mind your own crates.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Ignore him. The fishmongers of Dunnock Quay say whatever comes into their heads, and it is usually about me.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: He called you a gull, Inspector?

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: A nickname. I did not choose it and I will not discuss it.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Now. Corin Ashdale, twenty-four, clerk of the Net-Menders' Union. Last seen four nights ago.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: His boat, the Pale Heron, was found drifting off Skerrin Rock yesterday. Empty.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Then he is presumed drowned?

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: "Presumed" is a word for people who have stopped looking. We have not.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Walk with me. Say nothing to the press, and nothing to the family until I say so.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Understood, Inspector.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Four nights. And the boat came home without him.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: There you are! Come in, come in, mind the draught. The kettle's on.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Miss Fenwick, this is Constable Reeve. Constable, Miss Fenwick keeps our records.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Keeps them, scolds them, and feeds them. Welcome to Harrowmere, dear.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Thank you, Miss Fenwick. It is good to meet you.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Edda, please. Nobody's called me Miss Fenwick since the old harbourmaster retired.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: The young ones call me Mother Hen, because I fuss. You may as well, if you must.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: The Mooring Ledger, Edda. Reeve needs to see last month's entries.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Of course. Grey cabinet, third drawer down. The key sticks, so give it a jiggle.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: That is a great many berths. Did Mr. Ashdale work on these pages?

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Corin did the sums for the Net-Menders' Union and I checked them. Sweet boy. Careful with numbers, careless with his supper.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: He took it hard, you know, about the Pale Heron. Her paint was his father's.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Took what hard?

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Oh, the debts, dear. The boat was mortgaged to the mast. Most fishing families are.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Debts to whom, exactly?

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: The Union fund, mostly. He swore he'd pay it back in full.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Noted. Reeve, we will look at the fund accounts tomorrow.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: I would like to see the boat myself, Inspector.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Tomorrow. The tide is wrong today.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Wise. Skerrin Rock bites at the wrong tide.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Edda believes he may have taken the boat out in despair.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: I don't believe it, Dorian. I only fear it. There's a difference.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Yes. Quite.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: She calls him Dorian. Nobody else has dared.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Tea, everyone! Constable, sugar? You look as if you could use two.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: One, please. Thank you.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Put the cups down. Work first.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Work after tea, Dorian. A hungry constable finds nothing.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Reeve. Take the {item} from the evidence shelf. It came off the Pale Heron.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: A scarf, Inspector. Wet wool, a child's knitting pattern.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: That'd be Pippa's. Corin's little sister knitted it for him at Midwinter. Poor lamb.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: She's staying with Oswin Tarn, down by the Brine Steps. Be gentle with her.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: We shall see her this afternoon. Edda, keep the ledger safe.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Locked and watched, Dorian. Nobody touches it but me.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Day one. Harrowmere smells of tar and boiled cabbage.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Hollis speaks as if every word is billed by the syllable.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Facts: the boat came back empty, the mooring ring is a mile from where it should be, and the Union's accounts are in the grey cabinet.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Miss Fenwick is kind. Write that down, too. It might be the only kind thing today.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Questions for tomorrow: 1. Who tied the Pale Heron? 2. Why was Corin whistling?

units.speaker: FISHMONGER
units.source: Mackerel, still twitching! Two for a copper, three if you smile!

units.speaker: PASSERBY 1
units.source: Two for a copper? Yesterday it was four.

units.speaker: FISHMONGER
units.source: Yesterday there wasn't a gale coming. Take it or leave it, love.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Excuse me. Have you seen Corin Ashdale in the last few days?

units.speaker: FISHMONGER
units.source: The Union lad? Not since Tuesday. Bought a pound of herring, paid in coin, whistled like a kettle.

units.speaker: FISHMONGER
units.source: Whistling. Doesn't sound like a boy about to throw himself in the water, does it?

units.speaker: PASSERBY 2
units.source: Don't go asking that. Folk say the Pale Heron is cursed.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Cursed how?

units.speaker: PASSERBY 2
units.source: Don't ask me. Ask old Tarn. He knows every ghost on the quay.

units.speaker: PASSERBY 3
units.source: Make way! Cart coming through, make way!

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Reeve. The chandler next. We need the rope receipts.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Morning, Inspector. The usual, or is this business?

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Both. Two fathoms of grey line, and do not charge me the tourist price.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Tourist price! For you it's the honest price, which is rare enough around here.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: And who's this? New blood? Welcome, miss. Anything you need, I've got it or I'll find it.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Thank you. I need a notebook with a waterproof cover, please.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Good choice. That one's two silver, but for a Tidewatch lass, one and a half.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: That is very kind of you. I will take it.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Anything else for you, Constable? Bootlaces? Lamp oil? A good knot-book?

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: That is all, thank you.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Mind how you go. And if you see the Ashdale girl, tell her the aniseed sweets are on me.

units.speaker: DOCKHAND
units.source: All hands to the quay! The cargo's in!

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: Are you the lady who's going to find Cor?

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: I am going to try. What is your name?

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: Pippa Ashdale. I'm nine and three quarters.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: Grander Tarn says never talk to strangers, but you're Tidewatch, so you're only half a stranger.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Pippa! Come away from the lass. She's working.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: She's not working, she's standing.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Standing is working, when you wear that coat.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Tarn's the name. Oswin. Most call me Grander, though I'm nobody's grandfather.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Mr. Tarn, sir, I would like to ask you about the Pale Heron.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Would you, now? Sit, lass. These steps are hard on old bones.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: That boat never came loose on her own. Corin tied his bowline the Harrowmere way, left over right. I taught him myself.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: The knot on her mooring ring was right over left. A stranger's knot.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: A stranger's knot. Are you certain?

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: I've been certain of three things in seventy-eight years. Tides, taxes and knots.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Pippa, I promise I will do everything I can.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: That's not a promise. That's what grown-ups say instead of one.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: I do not know yet. But I will always tell you the truth.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: Cor says the truth is the only thing that floats.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: He's a clever lad. Too clever for his own good, some say.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Sorrel left something for you. Here, {item}.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: Aniseed! Yuck! ...Thank you. I'll give it to the gulls.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Pippa, home. Your supper's cooling.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: Bye, lady constable! Don't let Mister Gull scare you!

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Mister Gull?

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: She means Hollis. The whole quay calls him the Old Gull. He pretends not to hear.

units.speaker: TOWN CRIER
units.source: Hear ye, hear ye, Harrowmere! The Tidewatch seeks word of Corin Ashdale, clerk, last seen at Dunnock Quay!

units.speaker: TOWN CRIER
units.source: Anyone with knowledge, speak to the Tidewatch office, and speak soon.

units.speaker: TOWN CRIER
units.source: The Greywater Ferry makes her last crossing at dusk. The Brindle Gale is expected by morning!

units.speaker: TOWN CRIER
units.source: Secure your nets, your shutters and your children, good people!

units.speaker: PASSERBY 2
units.source: Last crossing. Then we're shut in, with a boy gone missing.

units.speaker: PASSERBY 1
units.source: Hush. You'll frighten the little ones.

units.speaker: CROWD
units.source: Shame on the Tidewatch! Find him!

units.speaker: GULL LAMP RADIO
units.source: This is the Gull Lamp, Skerrin Rock, signing on for the evening. Visibility poor, wind rising from the north-west.

units.speaker: GULL LAMP RADIO
units.source: All vessels are advised to stay in harbour. The Fogbell will ring on the hour until further notice.

units.speaker: GULL LAMP RADIO
units.source: Anyone with news of Corin Ashdale, of Dunnock Quay, may leave word with the keeper at first light.

units.speaker: GULL LAMP RADIO
units.source: That is all from the Gull Lamp. Keep your lanterns trimmed, Harrowmere.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: The Fogbell rings on the hour. Remember that.
HARROWMERE GAZETTE — Thursday Edition
PALE HERON FOUND ADRIFT
The fishing boat Pale Heron, property of the late Ansel Ashdale, was found drifting off Skerrin Rock on Wednesday morning, her sails furled and her cabin dry.

Her owner's son, Corin Ashdale, 24, clerk of the Net-Menders' Union, has not been seen since Saturday night.
The Tidewatch asks anyone with information to come forward.
Harbour folk are reminded that the Brindle Gale is expected within the week. Ferries may be suspended without notice.
ALSO: Lowtide Market reopens Friday. Mackerel, two for a copper.

units.speaker: GULL LAMP RADIO
units.source: Gull Lamp to all of Harrowmere. The Brindle Gale has turned early. Landfall at dawn.

units.speaker: GULL LAMP RADIO
units.source: Greywater Ferry is suspended. Repeat, the ferry is suspended until the wind drops below gale force.

units.speaker: GULL LAMP RADIO
units.source: If you hear the Fogbell ring out of turn, do not come looking. Stay where you are.

units.speaker: TOWN CRIER
units.source: You heard the lamp, good people! Doors barred, lamps low, and keep to the Union hall if your roof is thin!

units.speaker: PASSERBY 3
units.source: Hall's open? Then I'm bringing the cat.

units.speaker: PASSERBY 1
units.source: Bring the whole street. Hetty won't turn anyone away.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: The tide-glass in the office dropped like a stone overnight. Reeve. Report.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: I checked the three mooring rings, Inspector. The knot Mr. Tarn described is on the middle one. Right over left.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: And the fund accounts?

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Miss Fenwick says the Mooring Ledger is in order, but I have not yet compared it with the Union's own books.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Then you will do so when the gale has passed. Walk faster, the wind is turning.

units.speaker: GUARD 1
units.source: Inspector! Quay's closing. Orders from the harbour board, nobody on the outer pier.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: I know my own orders, Guard.

units.speaker: GUARD 1
units.source: Sorry, sir. And who is she?

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Constable Reeve, Tidewatch.

units.speaker: GUARD 1
units.source: Then you'd best get her indoors, sir. First gust took a man's hat clean to Skerrin Rock.

units.speaker: DOCKHAND
units.source: Hey! You two! Tie that skiff down or lose her!

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Reeve. The skiff. Ropes.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Right over left, Inspector, or left over right?

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: ...Left over right. The Harrowmere way.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Of course. Done.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Hm. Not entirely hopeless, Constable.
Rain hammers the shutters. A few dozen people crowd the hall with blankets and lanterns.

units.speaker: HETTY
units.source: Settle, everyone! Blankets on the left, lamps on the right, and nobody lights anything near the nets!

units.speaker: TOBY
units.source: Hetty, there's a hole in the north roof the size of a barrel.

units.speaker: HETTY
units.source: Then put a barrel under it, Toby. We've done it before.

units.speaker: TOBY
units.source: That's your answer? A barrel?

units.speaker: HETTY
units.source: That's my answer, and it's a good one. Go on.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Sit, sit, everyone. I've brought the big pot. There's enough soup for the whole hall.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: Mother Hen! Can I have the end of the loaf?

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: The end of the loaf, and the butter, and a blanket for your knees. Come here, lamb.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Eddie girl, you spoil that child.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Somebody has to, Oswin. Eat your soup and stop being clever.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Miss Fenwick, if I may. Chair Vale, a word before the soup.

units.speaker: HETTY
units.source: Inspector. Make it quick, I've got ninety people to dry out.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Corin Ashdale. When did you last speak with him?

units.speaker: HETTY
units.source: Saturday afternoon. Here, in this room. He asked me for the Union's account books.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Did he say why, Chair Vale?

units.speaker: HETTY
units.source: Call me Hetty, nobody says Chair Vale unless there's a fine coming. He said the numbers didn't match.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Which numbers?

units.speaker: HETTY
units.source: The fund. Berth fees, pension dues. He said six hundred silver were missing, and he wanted to find where it went before he told the members.

units.speaker: TOBY
units.source: Six hundred? That's a year's pension for half of this hall!

units.speaker: HETTY
units.source: Toby, keep your voice down. That is exactly why he wanted to tell us properly.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Six hundred. Aye, that's a number a man might be quiet about.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Mr. Orme. You quarrelled with Ashdale last week.

units.speaker: TOBY
units.source: Who told you that?

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Half the quay. Answer the question.

units.speaker: TOBY
units.source: We argued about dues, that's all. He's my friend. He was my friend. Is my friend!

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: Cor is still your friend, Toby. You said so at the fair.

units.speaker: TOBY
units.source: I know, Pip. I know. Sorry I shouted.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Hmph. Shouting won't find the boy. A good lamp might. Anyone short of oil, I've a barrel in the back.

units.speaker: HETTY
units.source: Sorrel, you're a saint.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: I'm a shopkeeper. Saints don't send invoices, Hetty.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Toby, where were you on Saturday night?

units.speaker: TOBY
units.source: Mending nets on the far side of the quay. Ask anyone, I was there until midnight.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: He was. I fell asleep on his bench, and he lent me his coat.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Thank you, Mr. Tarn. That is useful.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Hetty, who else knew Corin was looking at the accounts?

units.speaker: HETTY
units.source: Nobody. I told him not to speak of it until we had more.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: I knew a little, dear. He asked me for the old mooring sheets, that's all. I thought he was tidying.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Tidying, Miss Fenwick?

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Corin tidied when he was worried. It was his way.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Noted. Reeve, write it all down.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: I already am, Inspector.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Good.
A gust slams the shutters. The lanterns gutter, then steady.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: Lady constable, is that the sea knocking?

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: It is only wind, Pippa. Wind knocks, but it cannot come in.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: The sea can come in, though. It came in last year. We had a fish in the pantry.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Aye, a fine fat bream. She named him Gerald.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: He was a good fish.

units.speaker: PASSERBY 1
units.source: Is it true, what they say? That the Fogbell rang itself on Skerrin Rock last night?

units.speaker: PASSERBY 2
units.source: The keeper swears he never touched it.

units.speaker: HETTY
units.source: Quiet, you two. Don't spook the children.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: It rings when the wind finds the rope. Always has. Don't fret, Hetty.

units.speaker: TOBY
units.source: Wind doesn't ring on the hour, Grander.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Doesn't it? Wind has done stranger things.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Mr. Tarn, you fish those waters. Could a man survive a night on Skerrin Rock?

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: In the old fogbell chamber? Dry as a biscuit, up the stairs. If he had food and a candle.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: The chamber. Inspector, we should check it when the weather clears.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: We shall consider it. For now, we eat.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: There! Hear that? The sensible man speaks. Bowls, everyone, bowls!

units.speaker: HETTY
units.source: Everybody listen up! Soup first, stories after. Pass your bowls to the front!

units.speaker: CROWD
units.source: Thank you, Mother Hen!

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Oh, go on with you.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Constable, a word. Strictly between us.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Of course, Miss Brant.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Last week I sold a length of heavy chain and a padlock. Paid in coin. I don't ask names, it's bad for trade.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Who bought them?

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: That's the thing. I can't quite see the face. Wind and hood and rain, that evening.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Would you know them again?

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Maybe. Maybe not. I'll think on it. Don't you tell the Inspector yet. He frightens a woman into forgetting.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: I will say nothing until you are ready.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Reeve. What are you whispering about with the chandler?

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Lamp oil, Inspector. The price has risen.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Hm.

units.speaker: TOBY
units.source: Does anyone else smell smoke?

units.speaker: HETTY
units.source: Toby, if that's your pipe, I'll drown it myself.

units.speaker: TOBY
units.source: It isn't my pipe!

units.speaker: DOCKHAND
units.source: Fire! No, no, sorry, it's the soup! Somebody burned the soup!

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: I did not burn the soup. I let it develop character.

units.speaker: HETTY
units.source: Ha! Everyone, calm down. It's the soup.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: Can I still have some?

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: The top of the pot is perfect, lamb. Here.
The hall settles. The wind drops to a long, low moan.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Inspector, may I say something?

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: You may.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: If Corin found six hundred silver missing, someone else knows he found it.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: That is a supposition. But it is not a stupid one.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Thank you, Inspector.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Do not thank me for the obvious. Go and sit with the child, she is shivering.

units.speaker: DOCKHAND
units.source: Inspector! Constable! The Pale Heron has torn her moorings and capsized against the Brine Steps!

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Coats. Now.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: There! The hull, against the steps. Inspector, the cabin door is open.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Careful. The planks are slick. Hold the lantern higher.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Poor girl. Forty years she carried that family, and now look at her.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Mr. Tarn, you should not be out here. It is not safe.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Not safe, she says. Lass, I've been out in worse than this at your age and in a leaky bucket.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Mr. Tarn. Stand clear of the hull, please.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: I'll stand where I please, Dorian Hollis, and you know why.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: ...As you wish. Reeve, the locker under the bunk.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: A hidden locker behind the bunk panel, split open by the waves. A pea-coat, wet through, and a letter in the inside pocket, sealed in oilcloth.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Give it here.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: It is addressed to Pippa Ashdale, Inspector. Not to us.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: It may be evidence.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: With respect, it is also a child's letter. May I read it first, and decide what the child can bear?

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: ...You may. Briefly.

units.speaker: DOCKHAND
units.source: Another gust! Everybody back from the Steps!

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Inspector, hold the {item} while I read under the awning.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Hold it away from the water, Constable.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Night two. The sea gave back a coat and a letter, and took nothing in return.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Corin wrote: "I've found where the money goes. I'm going to tell someone I trust tonight."

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Someone he trusts. So he told someone. Then he vanished.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: I should feel clever. I feel cold.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Oswin says a man could survive a night in the fogbell chamber. A night. Not four.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Check the chamber at first light. If the gale lets me.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Pippa, do you have a moment? I found something that belongs to you.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: Is it Cor's? It is! It's got my name on it! He draws my name with a loop on the P.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: He does. May I sit with you while you read it?

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: Only if you don't tell Mother Hen I was up late.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Too late, lamb. I've got ears like a bat. Come here, both of you, you'll catch your death.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: Cor says: "Pip, I'll be home soon. Feed Gerald's ghost a crumb." That's our joke!

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: He sounds like he intended to come back.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Of course he did, dear. Of course. Don't read too much into a letter, now.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: Lady constable? Is Cor in the sea?

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: I do not think so. I think someone is hiding him, or holding him.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: Then you have to find him before the tide goes out. Cor says the tide takes things.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: I will find him, Pippa. I promise.

units.speaker: GULL LAMP RADIO
units.source: Gull Lamp, Skerrin Rock, midnight bulletin. Gale at peak. Waves breaking over the causeway.

units.speaker: GULL LAMP RADIO
units.source: Note to the harbour: the Fogbell has rung thrice off the hour. The keeper is checking the rope.

units.speaker: MORROW
units.source: Gull Lamp, this is the keeper. The rope is frayed, not cut. It rings with the wind. That is all. Do not cross.

units.speaker: GULL LAMP RADIO
units.source: End of bulletin. Keep warm, Harrowmere.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: The wind. Twice now, the wind. I do not like it.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Nor do I, Inspector.
Dear Pip,
If you're reading this, I'm probably late for supper again. Don't tell Grander Tarn.
I've found out something that's been bothering me for weeks. Numbers don't lie, but people can make them say the wrong thing.

I'm going to tell someone I trust tonight. If it goes well, I'll be home by the first bell.
If it doesn't...
...well, feed Gerald's ghost a crumb, and keep the red scarf warm for me.

Love,
Cor
TIDEWATCH NOTICE — GALE SEASON
1. The outer pier is closed whenever the Gull Lamp flies two red lanterns.
2. Skiffs must be tied with two knots, left over right, and registered with the Mooring Ledger.
3. Anyone found on Skerrin Rock without the keeper's leave will be fined.
By order of the Harrowmere Tidewatch.

units.speaker: GUARD 1
units.source: Halt! State your... oh. Inspector. Morning, sir.

units.speaker: GUARD 2
units.source: Morning, Inspector. Rough night. Roof's off the lamp store.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Then fix it. Reeve, with me.

units.speaker: GUARD 2
units.source: Is that the new one? She's got a stern face for a rookie.

units.speaker: GUARD 1
units.source: Shh. She can hear you.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: I can, Guard. Good morning.

units.speaker: GUARD 2
units.source: Ah. Sorry, Constable. Mornin'.

units.speaker: GUARD 1
units.source: Don't mind him. He's been on the gate since the old harbourmaster's day.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Stop gossiping, both of you. Has anyone been in or out of the office since last night?

units.speaker: GUARD 1
units.source: Only Miss Fenwick, sir. Came at dawn to light the stove.

units.speaker: GUARD 2
units.source: Looked fair worn out. Her shawl was soaked.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: She works too hard. Open the gate.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Oh, Dorian, dear, I can't tell you. I came in to light the stove and found the cabinet open.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Open? I thought only you had the key.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: I did. I do! The lock hasn't been forced. Whoever it was, they knew the jiggle.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: The jiggle, Miss Fenwick?

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: The trick of the key, dear. It sticks. Half the quay knows it.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Half the quay has been in this office?

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Not half. But you'd be surprised who pops in for a cup of tea.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: What is missing, exactly?

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Eleven pages. All of them from the autumn quarter, the berth fees.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: The same quarter Corin was investigating.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Oh. Oh, I hadn't thought of that. How dreadful.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Pardon the state of me. I've been up all night with my old grey shawl and that dreadful stove.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Edda. Sit. Reeve, fetch her a chair.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: At once, Inspector.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: You're kind, both of you. Truly. I'm sorry, I'm quite undone.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Who has been asking after the ledger this week?

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Well, Toby Orme popped in, twice. Said he needed the Union copies. He seemed rather fretful.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Toby was mending nets until midnight on Saturday. Tarn vouches for it.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Did he? Oh, good. Good. I'd hate to think it was him.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Miss Fenwick, did Corin say anything about the ledger before he went missing?

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Only that he'd found a mistake. He wouldn't say where. He was the careful sort, you know.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Thank you. I will look at the empty slots in the cabinet, if I may.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Of course, dear. Mind your sleeves, the lacquer's wet.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Reeve. The padlock on that drawer. Is it new?

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: It is, Inspector. The brass is bright. Whoever fitted it did so recently.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Then someone wanted that cabinet secure. Or wanted it to look secure.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Day five. Eleven pages gone, and a brand-new padlock on a cabinet that was never locked before.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Sorrel sold a chain and a padlock to a hooded stranger. A coincidence? I do not believe in those, not here.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Suspects: Toby (no alibi problem), Hetty (fund chair), Sorrel (the lock). Everyone else is a friend.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Hollis is wrong to trust no one. And I am wrong to trust everyone.

units.speaker: FISHMONGER
units.source: Herring! Last of the stock before the ferry comes back! Don't dawdle!

units.speaker: PASSERBY 1
units.source: Is it true the Pale Heron was cut loose by hand?

units.speaker: FISHMONGER
units.source: I heard it was a ghost. The sea took him, they say, and gave back the boat out of spite.

units.speaker: PASSERBY 2
units.source: A ghost! Honestly. It was somebody with a knife and a grudge.

units.speaker: PASSERBY 3
units.source: Somebody in a grey shawl, I heard. Lurking on the Steps.

units.speaker: FISHMONGER
units.source: Grey shawls! Half of Harrowmere owns a grey shawl. My mother owned three.

units.speaker: PASSERBY 1
units.source: And I heard the Old Gull has finally met his match. Look at him following her around.

units.speaker: FISHMONGER
units.source: Other way round, love. She's the one with the notebook.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Excuse me, may I ask you something?

units.speaker: FISHMONGER
units.source: Course. Mackerel, two for a copper.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Not fish, thank you. Did you see anyone near the Pale Heron on Saturday night?

units.speaker: FISHMONGER
units.source: Saturday? Dark as a bucket. I saw a skiff leave the pier around ten. Tidewatch colours, I thought.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Tidewatch colours? Are you sure?

units.speaker: FISHMONGER
units.source: Grey hull, brass fittings. Aye. Anyone can paint a boat.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Close the door, then. I don't like the draught or the questions.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Miss Brant, you sold a length of heavy chain and a padlock last week.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: I sell chain every week. It's a chandlery, Inspector.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Constable Reeve will take it from here.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Thank you, Inspector. Miss Brant, thank you for seeing us.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Seeing you. Hm. As if I had a choice.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Miss Brant, a boy is missing and you are holding something back. Who bought the chain?

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Don't you bark at me in my own back room, girl.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Fine. Fine! A customer, in the rain. That's all I said.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: That is not all you said on the night of the gale.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: I said I couldn't see the face. And that's true!

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Miss Brant, you were kind to me on my first day. I would like to be kind in return. What worries you?

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Kind. Hmph. You'll go far, miss, or get yourself killed.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: What worries me is that I know the customer, somewhere. I just can't pull it up. It's like a word on the tip of your tongue.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Take your time.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: It was after closing. Raining sideways. The customer came to the shutter, not the door.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Man or woman?

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: A hood. Grey, or a shawl, I couldn't swear which. And a small voice. Polite.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Polite how?

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: "Thank you ever so much, dear." Said it twice. Left coin on the counter and didn't wait for change.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: A customer who does not wait for change. Remarkable.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: That's what I thought. Nobody in Harrowmere skips their change.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Here is your own sales receipt for the chain. Does the date jog your memory?

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Third of the month. A Saturday. Aye, the night Corin went.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: I wrote it down because I charged double. The gale was already coming. Everyone was buying.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Double. Of course you did.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: The Pale Heron was tied with a knot only an outsider would use. Did anyone ask you for a knot-book?

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: A knot-book? Aye! I sold one that week, second-hand. Same customer, I think. I'd forgotten.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: She wanted the one with the fancy ones. Right over left, she said. For a nephew.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: She.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: I said she, didn't I? Did I say she?

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Miss Brant, think carefully. Anything else about the voice?

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Lavender. She smelled of lavender soap. And her hands were soft, no nets.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Thank you, Miss Brant. You have helped more than you know.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Don't thank me. Just don't tell Hetty I'm talking to the Tidewatch. She'll call me a collaborator.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Your name stays out of it.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Good. Now, will either of you buy something? Standing around makes a shop look empty.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: A box of matches, Miss Brant. I will pay the honest price.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Honest price, then. And thank you, Inspector. Anything else?
The tide is low. The quay is empty but for two lanterns.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: You are not asleep, Constable.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Neither are you, Inspector.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: I do not sleep during an open case. It is a habit and a flaw.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: May I ask you something, Inspector?

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: You may ask.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Why did Oswin Tarn say "and you know why" to you on the Steps?

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: ...Because he is the only man in Harrowmere who remembers Wendell Rusk.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Wendell was my partner. Fifteen years ago, on a case very like this one, a man vanished from the quay.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: I followed a lead to Skerrin Rock, ignored the tide and ignored Wendell. He went in after the man. The sea kept him.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: I am sorry, Inspector.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Do not be. I am telling you so you understand my rules. I do not scold because I am cruel. I scold because I am frightened.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Frightened of what?

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Of having a second person to bury.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: You were right to make us wait for the tide yesterday.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: That was luck. You, on the other hand, saw the knot before I did. I should have said so at once.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: I am saying it now. Well done, Reeve.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Thank you, Inspector. It means a great deal.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: ...Stop calling me Inspector at midnight. It makes me feel like a statue.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Then what should I call you?

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Dorian. If you must call me something.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: You are not as terrifying as you pretend to be, Dorian.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: ...Dorian. Well. That is the first time in fifteen years anyone has said it without a warrant in their hand.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: I will let it pass. This once.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: And you are... {player}, is it not? I have been calling you "Constable" like a coward.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: {player}. Yes. Everyone at the academy called me Rookie.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Then we will have to do better than the academy. {player}.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Dorian.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Good. Now. Four nights, one boy. Tell me what you think of Miss Fenwick's grey shawl.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: I think Miss Fenwick is the kindest person in Harrowmere, and half the town owns a shawl like it.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Half the town. Yes. I suppose that is true.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: You do not sound convinced.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: I am not convinced of anything. I am only awake.

units.speaker: TOWN CRIER
units.source: Hear ye, Harrowmere! A reward of fifty silver, offered by the Net-Menders' Union, for any word of Corin Ashdale!

units.speaker: TOWN CRIER
units.source: The Greywater Ferry runs again at noon. All passengers must show their tickets, and their manners!

units.speaker: TOWN CRIER
units.source: Reminder: the outer pier remains closed, and Lowtide Market is open until dusk, rain or shine. The Tidewatch will fine trespassers.

units.speaker: PASSERBY 2
units.source: Fifty silver! I'd tell them my own mother's secrets for that.

units.speaker: PASSERBY 3
units.source: You'd tell them your mother's secrets for a mackerel.

units.speaker: GULL LAMP RADIO
units.source: Gull Lamp, Skerrin Rock, morning bulletin. Sea state moderate. The causeway opens at ten past eleven and closes at noon.

units.speaker: GULL LAMP RADIO
units.source: Visitors to the island must report to the keeper at the lower door. Not the upper door. The upper door is locked.

units.speaker: MORROW
units.source: This is the keeper. A reminder to all: the Fogbell chamber is closed. Do not climb the stair. Do not ring the bell. I will not say it again.

units.speaker: GULL LAMP RADIO
units.source: End of bulletin. Gull Lamp out.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Dorian, you have a crumb of toast on your collar.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: That is evidence of breakfast, not a crime.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: You had breakfast?

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Edda sent a basket. She said I looked "peaky." I have not looked peaky in thirty years.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: You looked peaky yesterday, Old Gull.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: I will have you know I am a lion in a gull's coat. And you, Rookie, are a menace.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: Mister Gull! Lady constable! Look, I made you a paper gull!

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: It has a very fine beak. Thank you, Miss Ashdale.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: It's for luck. Grander Tarn says luck is just hard work wearing a hat.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Then we will wear it proudly. Thank you, Pippa.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Mornin', you two. Meet me at the Brine Steps in twenty minutes. The tide's right. If you want Skerrin Rock, we leave within the hour.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Tarn, we will be ready in thirty minutes.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Make it twenty. The tide-glass says calm, but it lies on Tuesdays. The causeway shuts at noon.
{player} Reeve — Notebook, Day Five

Facts:
- Corin Ashdale vanished Saturday night.
- The Pale Heron was tied with a right-over-left knot.
- Eleven pages are gone from the Mooring Ledger.

Heard:
- A hooded customer bought chain, a padlock and a knot-book at Sorrel's.
- A grey Tidewatch-coloured skiff left the pier around ten.

Unknown:
- Who tied the knot?
- Who knows the jiggle of the cabinet key?
- Where was Corin going to "tell someone he trusts"?
Note to self: ask Oswin about the fogbell chamber. Do not forget the tide.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Sit low, both of you. The Rock doesn't like tall people.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: I am not afraid of the sea, Tarn.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Then why is your face the colour of porridge, Dorian?

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: He is seasick, Mr. Tarn. He has been seasick since the pier.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: I am thinking. That is how it looks.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Dorian, that is the worst excuse I have ever heard.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Rookie, one more word and I will make you row.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Ha! Listen to them. A fortnight ago she was "Inspector, yes sir, no sir."

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: A fortnight ago, he was "Constable Reeve, you are late."

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: I was right. You were late.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: She's got your number, Old Gull.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: I thought we agreed nobody calls me that.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: We agreed nothing of the kind.
Spray lifts over the bow. Skerrin Rock rises out of the grey, the Gull Lamp pale in the daylight.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: There she is. Forty years I've fished under that lamp and never once liked it.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Why not?

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: It watches. You can feel it, lad, even in daylight.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Mr. Tarn, is that the causeway?

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Aye. We've got an hour before the sea closes it. Mind the weed, it's slick as lard.

units.speaker: MORROW
units.source: State your business.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Inspector Hollis, Harrowmere Tidewatch. This is Constable Reeve. We have a warrant to search the island.

units.speaker: MORROW
units.source: Warrants don't climb stairs. Show me the paper.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Here, sir. Signed by the harbour board.

units.speaker: MORROW
units.source: Hm. Morrow, keeper. Visitors keep to the lower stair. No smoking. No shouting. No touching the lamp.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: We are looking for Corin Ashdale. Has he been here?

units.speaker: MORROW
units.source: Nobody's been here. The ferry stopped a week ago.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Then why does the Fogbell ring off the hour?

units.speaker: MORROW
units.source: Wind on the rope. I told the radio.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: The rope is frayed, you said. Not cut. Could we see it?

units.speaker: MORROW
units.source: It's in the chamber. The stair is locked. I lost the key in the gale.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Lost.

units.speaker: MORROW
units.source: Lost. I'm a lighthouse keeper, not a locksmith.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Come on, Morrow, you've known me thirty years. Let them climb.

units.speaker: MORROW
units.source: ...Lower stair only. And I'll be watching.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: The lower stair ends at the chamber door. Morrow cannot say we were not invited.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Dorian, listen. There. Tapping. Three short, two long.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: It is the wind on the rope.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: The wind does not tap in a pattern.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: ...No. No, it does not.

units.speaker: CORIN
units.source: Hello? Is somebody there? Please?

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Corin! Corin Ashdale! It's the Tidewatch!

units.speaker: CORIN
units.source: I knew it. I knew somebody would hear. I've been ringing for days.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Hold on, lad. Reeve, the door. There is a chain, and a padlock.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: The same heavy chain as Sorrel's shop, I would swear to it. And it is new brass.

units.speaker: CORIN
units.source: Don't touch the lock! She said she'd come back with the key. She said she'd... oh. Someone's on the stair!

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Dorian? Dorian, dear, are you up there? I followed the Tidewatch skiff!

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Edda? Stay where you are! This is not safe!

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: I couldn't bear to sit in that office, not knowing. I brought the spare key. I found it in the drawer.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Dorian. Nobody told her what the lock was for. She brought the right key anyway.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Not now, {player}.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Look, look, here it is. Let me, my hands are steady. The lock sticks. You have to jiggle it.

units.speaker: CORIN
units.source: She knows how to do it. She does it every time. Please. Please don't let her do it again.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: ...Edda. Stop.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Whatever is the matter, Dorian? The boy's frightened. Let me open it.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Miss Fenwick. Step away from the door.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Dear, you're shaking. Let me.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Step away, please.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Edda, why do you smell of lavender?

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Because I'm a woman who bathes, Dorian. What a silly question.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Sorrel Brant said the person who bought the chain smelled of lavender. And said "thank you ever so much, dear." Twice.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Half of Harrowmere says "dear." I say it to everyone.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: You said you found the cabinet open. You said whoever did it knew the jiggle. Nobody else on the quay is allowed in that office, Miss Fenwick. You told us so on the first day.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: "Nobody touches it but me." Those were your words, Edda.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Dorian. Thirty years.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: I know. That is why I am asking.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Edda Fenwick, you locked Corin Ashdale in the Fogbell chamber and cut the Pale Heron adrift. Say it.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Oh, you clever girl.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Yes. All right. Yes, I did.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Edda, you fed half this town. Whatever you did, there was a reason. Tell me.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: A reason! You see, Dorian? She understands.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: I did it, dear. All of it. And I would do it again.

units.speaker: CORIN
units.source: She's right outside, isn't she? Oh God. She brought me soup for two days.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: I did, didn't I? I never wanted him hungry.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Why, Edda? Why would you do this to a boy who trusted you?

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: The Union's pension fund was bleeding for ten years, Dorian. Ten! Wages, rents, my sister's care home. A few silver a month from phantom berths, and nobody ever missed it.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Then clever Corin counted. He came to me, to me, because he trusted me. And I thought... if he tells Hetty, the whole hall burns.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: So you burned him instead.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: I kept him warm, dear. I kept him fed. I was going to let him out when the audit season passed.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Eddie girl. You cut the lad's own boat loose to make him a drowned man.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Oswin, you of all people... I tied the knot the way my father taught me. The ferry way. Right over left. I forgot. I always forget that the Harrowmere way is left over right.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: That's how I knew, you wretched fool. I just didn't want to know.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Eleven pages. The cabinet. The padlock. The skiff with the grey hull. Edda, I let you hand me a cup of tea each morning.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Dorian. Don't. You'll make me cry, and then I'll have to make you more tea.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Give me the key.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: I think not, dear. The tide is turning. Do you hear it? The causeway is closing. In twenty minutes this stair floods to the third step.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: You would drown him?

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: I would rather not. But I would rather the Union did not burn. So.
She opens her hand. The brass key falls through the grating into the dark water below.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Edda!

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: There. It's out of everyone's hands now. Isn't that restful?

units.speaker: MORROW
units.source: Stand aside, Fenwick. I've got bolt cutters in the lamp room. It's about time someone climbed the upper stair.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Keeper Morrow! You said you had lost the key!

units.speaker: MORROW
units.source: I lied. Fenwick brought me that chain weeks ago and said the chamber was storing Union records. Told me to keep everyone out. I didn't ask why. I'm a fool, not a villain.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: We shall discuss that later. Cut it. Now.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Oh, but you can't be rid of me so easily, Dorian. I was your clerk when you were young. I know every secret of your office.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Then you will tell them to a judge, Fenwick.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: ...Fenwick. Not Edda. Not Mother Hen. How cold.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: You made it so, Miss Fenwick.

units.speaker: MORROW
units.source: Hold the lantern. Steady. I'll take the chain at the second link.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Water is coming through the grating. Hurry, Keeper!

units.speaker: CORIN
units.source: I can hear it! I can hear the sea!

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Corin, stand back from the door! Three steps back!

units.speaker: CORIN
units.source: I'm back! I'm back!
The cutters bite. The chain falls with a clang that rings through the whole tower.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Corin! Can you walk?

units.speaker: CORIN
units.source: I think so. My legs have forgotten how.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Lean on me. Reeve, take his other arm.

units.speaker: CORIN
units.source: Inspector Hollis? Constable? I'm so sorry. I should have gone to the Tidewatch. I went to her instead.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: You went to a friend. That is nothing to apologise for.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Oh, it's always nothing to apologise for, until it isn't.

units.speaker: GUARD 1
units.source: Inspector! The second skiff's at the pier! Tarn said you'd need us!

units.speaker: GUARD 2
units.source: Where is she? Where's Miss Fenwick? We're ordered to take her in, sir.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: On the stair. Gently, Guard. She is a prisoner, not a criminal in a story.

units.speaker: GUARD 2
units.source: Yes, sir. Miss Fenwick? If you'd come with us, please.

units.speaker: EDDA
units.source: Of course, young man. Mind my shawl, it's the only one I have left.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Time, lads! The causeway! Everybody into the boat or the sea will have the lot of us!

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Dorian, the water is at my knees!

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Then run, {player}! Run!

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: Cor! Cor! You're here! You're really here! I've been waiting on the Brine Steps all morning!

units.speaker: CORIN
units.source: Pip! Easy, easy, I'm made of glass right now.

units.speaker: PIPPA
units.source: I kept your scarf warm. And Gerald's ghost got his crumb. Every day.

units.speaker: CORIN
units.source: I knew you would. Come here, you little gull.

units.speaker: HETTY
units.source: Corin Ashdale, you owe this hall six hundred silver of explanations.

units.speaker: CORIN
units.source: I know, Hetty. I'll show every page. Starting with the ones Edda took.

units.speaker: HETTY
units.source: She took... oh. Oh, no. Not Edda.

units.speaker: TOBY
units.source: I never trusted that soup. No, I'm kidding. I'm so sorry, Cor.

units.speaker: FISHMONGER
units.source: Corin, lad! Come to Lowtide Market tomorrow and I'll give you a whole mackerel. Free, mind. Don't tell anyone.

units.speaker: SORREL
units.source: Free bandages for the boy, and a hot bun from my stall. And no, I won't send an invoice.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Lass. Rookie. You did well.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Thank you, Mr. Tarn. It was a good tie, in the end. Left over right.

units.speaker: OSWIN
units.source: Aye. Harrowmere style.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: {player}. A word.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Dorian?

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: I owe you an apology. For the first week, and the Inspector business, and the porridge-faced seasickness.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: You are forgiven for two of those. The third, I am keeping for blackmail.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: You are a better detective than I was at your age.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: You are a better liar than I am at any age. You said you were not seasick.

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: I will deny this conversation.

units.speaker: TOWN CRIER
units.source: Hear ye, Harrowmere! Corin Ashdale has been found alive and well on Skerrin Rock!

units.speaker: TOWN CRIER
units.source: The Tidewatch thanks all who searched. The Greywater Ferry runs on time, as promised!

units.speaker: CROWD
units.source: Hooray for the Tidewatch! Hooray for the Old Gull!

units.speaker: HOLLIS
units.source: Ignore them.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: I could not possibly. Old Gull.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Last page for now. The tide is going out and the Gull Lamp is lit.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Edda Fenwick sat three feet from me for a fortnight and handed me tea. I never saw it.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Kindness is not evidence. Neither is its absence.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Corin will be fine. Pippa has already redrawn the Fogbell, with a face.

units.speaker: REEVE
units.source: Dorian says the posting here is permanent. I think I will unpack.

units.speaker: GULL LAMP RADIO
units.source: This is the Gull Lamp, Skerrin Rock, signing on. The sea is calm and the Fogbell is silent.

units.speaker: GULL LAMP RADIO
units.source: A message for the harbour: Harrowmere, you may sleep.
Berth fees, autumn quarter: 311 silver paid, 208 recorded.
Eleven ghost berths, all in the same hand. Moorings that do not exist at Dunnock Quay.
If I tell Hetty, the hall will split. If I tell nobody, the fund dies. I'll ask someone steady first.
HARROWMERE GAZETTE — Special Edition
MISSING CLERK FOUND ALIVE ON SKERRIN ROCK
Corin Ashdale, 24, was rescued from the old fogbell chamber of the Gull Lamp as the tide closed the causeway. He is weak but well.
